mission: Ben processes the Jacen recognition and Desh's warning. The Lie is cracking — solitary control may be the disease, not the cure. But Ben doesn't yet have an alternative.
why_now: End of second pinch point — Ben must carry the recognition into the final chapters before the second plot point
conflict: Internal reckoning: Ben's Lie (self-reliance as safety) is being challenged by evidence that his approach mirrors the failing pattern. He needs to lead differently — but how?
turning_point: Ben thinks about his mother. Not Mara the Jedi, Mara the pragmatist — the woman who would have said 'stop thinking about whether you're worthy and start thinking about what works.' The thought doesn't solve anything. It changes the angle.
opening_hook: Ben slides down the corridor bulkhead until he's sitting on the deck plates, legs stretched across the narrow passage — the first time on this trip he's let his body admit how tired he is
closing_hook: The resonance note in the Codex files. Gavran wrote: 'We lacked the will or the trust.' Ben has been reading this as 'we weren't brave enough.' He re-reads it now: 'We couldn't trust each other enough.' Different emphasis. Different problem. Maybe a different solution.
emotional_trajectory: Exhausted honesty -> memory of Mara -> the angle shift on the resonance note

stakes.personal: Ben's arc approaching moment of truth — the Lie cracking but not yet broken
stakes.interpersonal: The memory of Mara as a different model of leadership
stakes.external: The resonance note becoming important — the solution's shape emerging

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — corridor, alone, night cycle
sensory_details: Cold deck plates through his trousers; the bulkhead's vibration against his spine; the ship's ambient hum; the datapad balanced on his knees with the Codex notes glowing; Mara's memory — not mystical, just a mother's pragmatism; the resonance note's words rearranging themselves in his mind
action_beats: Ben slides down the corridor bulkhead and sits on the cold deck plates, legs stretched across the narrow passage
Ben pulls up the Codex notes on his datapad and scrolls to Gavran's resonance annotation
Ben reads the note again — 'we lacked the will or the trust' — and the emphasis shifts under his eyes
notes: The Mara reference should be brief and practical — not mystical dead-parent wisdom. Just: 'What would Mom do? Stop philosophizing and solve the problem.' Ben's re-reading of the resonance note is the critical micro-turn.
